task.description: WF-02 Step 3b: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's REQ-422 (MOB-5) coverage. Decompose every multi-clause/'and'-joined acceptance criterion independently (per the ISS-0880 lesson — do not accept TEST-DESIGNER's own coverage table at face value) and confirm each clause's assertion would genuinely fail if that specific clause alone were violated, by reading the actual test files, not just the spec's narrative.
acceptance_criteria: Every clause of AC1-AC10 (as decomposed in the dispatch) verified against the actual test file/assertion, not against test/specs/REQ-422.md's own claim
No @tag skip on a MUST-covering test without a passing counterpart
No 'TODO: implement test' left in the spec
Test fixtures use per-test-unique data / no cross-test pollution
No hardcoded secrets/connection strings (sentinel fixture strings excluded per dispatch note)
PASS/FAIL verdict with next_action, handoff linted/committed/pushed

result.summary:
Independently re-derived, not copied from TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary. Checked out feature/WF02-REQ422-20260929 at commit 3cf4b6b8. Read test/specs/REQ-422.md, then opened and read the actual Dart source of every test file it cites: apps/mobile/test/guards/token_storage_boundary_guard_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/security/token_redaction_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/security/transport_policy_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/guards/android_manifest_security_guard_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/guards/ios_ats_guard_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/bootstrap/tenant_switch_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/auth/audience_scoping_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/design_system/masked_reveal_text_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/support/fake_secure_storage_platform.dart.

Decomposed AC1-AC10 clause by clause per the dispatch and checked each against the real assertion, not the spec's narrative claim:

AC1 (1a/1b/1c/1d): checkTokenStorageBoundary is a pure function fed in-memory fixture maps. 1a's self-test constructs a fixture importing flutter_secure_storage outside lib/auth/auth.dart and asserts exactly one violation naming that file — would fail if the sanctioned-path check were removed or widened. 1b's two ADDED self-tests independently confirmed: one fixture under lib/auth/ importing shared_preferences asserts a violation naming 'shared_preferences' in its kind string (would fail if that branch were deleted or the regex broken), and a second fixture importing shared_preferences OUTSIDE lib/auth/+lib/api/ asserts zero violations (would fail if the check were accidentally made global instead of scoped) -- this is a genuine two-sided clause proof, not a single assertion. 1c's self-test requires BOTH dart:io import AND File( construction under lib/api/ (conjunctive, verified in the regex logic itself) and asserts exactly one violation. 1d is satisfied structurally: all self-tests are pure fixture-driven, independent of the real tree, so they test the checker's own logic. Real-tree assertion additionally proves the real lib/ has no violations today. All four sub-clauses verified as independently falsifiable.

AC2 (2a/2b/2c): 2a/2b exercised end-to-end through the real runTenantBootstrap + ApiClient.get with a debugPrint override capturing all output, sentinels SECRET-TOKEN-SENTINEL and SECRET-REFRESH-SENTINEL both injected via FakeAppAuthAdapter's token response, both asserted absent from captured output -- this would fail if the redaction path were removed or the interceptor chain skipped. Additionally independently unit-tested via RedactingLogInterceptor with a real Dio pipeline (Authorization-header case, token-endpoint-body case) -- confirmed the header case adds the header via an InterceptorsWrapper BEFORE the redacting interceptor (FIFO order comment verified correct against Dio semantics) so the redaction is actually exercised, not vacuously passing because no header was ever set. 2c: debugPrint dynamically captured; developer.log(/bare print( statically proven absent via regex on the real lib/api+lib/auth source (verified regex is a negative lookbehind, would not false-positive on 'sprint(' etc.); third-party logger package absence independently confirmed by reading pubspec.yaml directly (grep for logger/logging/pretty_dio_logger names found nothing) and by the file's own checkNoForbiddenLoggingPackage self-test. All three clauses independently falsifiable.

AC3 (3a-3e): checkAndroidManifestSecurity takes three raw XML strings, single-purpose regex/string checks per clause. 3a asserted directly against manifest content, self-test constructs a manifest fixture omitting usesCleartextTraffic and confirms the specific violation fires. 3b checked via a base-config regex against the main network-security-config file content directly (not the debug one -- confirmed by argument name mainNetworkSecurityConfigXml and separate debugNetworkSecurityConfigXml parameter, so 3b and 3d/3e cannot be conflated). 3c is a direct substring check on allowBackup="false". 3d is structurally enforced by construction: the checker reads exactly the main and debug config file contents as two separate parameters and applies _domainConfigCleartextTrue independently to each -- main must have zero matches, debug must have exactly one -- so there is no third file path the checker could silently accept a violation under. 3e's self-test adds a third domain (evil.example.com) to the debug config's existing two legitimate ones and asserts the checker's symmetric-difference-against-{10.0.2.2,localhost} check fires -- this specifically proves 'only these two' rather than 'at least these two'. All five sub-clauses independently verified as falsifiable, matching the spec's claims exactly.

AC4: command-execution evidence re-read directly from handoffs/WF02-REQ422-20260929/step-02b-mobile-dev.json (not re-executed, no Android build toolchain available in this environment either) -- confirmed the quoted aapt dump output supports both the usesCleartextTraffic=0x0 clause and the resolved network-security-config resource (res/8G.xml) showing only a base-config with cleartextTrafficPermitted=0x0 and no domain-config element, exactly as TEST-DESIGNER's spec states. This AC is documented, per WF-02 convention (REQ-420 precedent), as command-execution evidence rather than a Dart unit test; no further verification possible without a real Android build on this host.

AC5 (5a-5f): table-driven checkTransportPolicyDecisions covers 5c/5d/5e/5f in one table (https allowed both, 10.0.2.2/localhost allowed debug-only, evil.example.com rejected both) -- a regression toward 'reject everything' or 'allow everything' would fail multiple rows simultaneously, closing the vacuous-pass risk the spec claims. 5a's test asserts both throwsA(isA<DioException>()) AND fakeAdapter.requests.isEmpty -- verified the interceptor (_transportPolicyInterceptorForTest) calls handler.reject BEFORE handler.next, so the fake adapter genuinely never sees the request; this is not merely 'an exception was thrown for some other reason'. 5b's test asserts appAuthAdapter.callCount == 0 specifically, proving the OIDC step is never entered, not just that bootstrap failed for some other reason. 5e is exercised at both the Dio-interceptor level (fakeAdapter.requests has length 1, i.e. the call was actually made, not merely 'no exception') and the bootstrap/realm_url level (appAuthAdapter.callCount == 1). All six sub-clauses independently verified.

AC6 (6a/6b): checkInfoPlistAts is a pure string-scan function; 6a's two self-tests (fires on NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true, passes on =false) close the vacuous-pass risk explicitly -- a checker that always returns no-violations would fail the first self-test. 6b's deferral statement verified present verbatim in the test file's header comment and cross-checked against MOBILE-DEV's step-02b-mobile-dev.json result.summary -- both state the Windows-host iOS deferral. Both sub-clauses verified.

AC7 (7a/7b): 7a's tenant_switch_test.dart drives the real top-level switchTenant/logout functions and BootstrapController methods (not a reimplementation) against a real TenantTokenStore backed by FakeSecureStoragePlatform; asserts tokenStore.read(_realmA) is null after switching to beta, and a subsequent request attaches ONLY the beta token (checked both the specific header value 'Bearer token-beta' and containsKey('Authorization') is true) -- this closes the sub-case of 'A's token silently reused' as well as 'no token attached at all'. 7b's audience_scoping_test.dart deliberately stores a token under realm B's key whose idToken iss claims realm A (a fixture-level conflict production code would never itself create, exactly as the test's own comment states) and asserts the bearer interceptor's Authorization header is never attached to the outgoing request -- this fails closed. A third case (matching iss) and a fourth (undeterminable iss, fails open by design) are also asserted, so the fail-closed behavior is not a side effect of always rejecting. The reimplemented interceptor helper (_bearerInterceptorForTest) is flagged as an accepted pre-existing pattern (private closures cannot be imported); the decision logic it calls into (issuerOf, TenantTokenStore) is the real production code, and issuerOf itself is independently unit-tested (round-trip, idToken-preference, accessToken-fallback, malformed-token-never-throws) directly in the same file -- so this is not a case of testing a reimplementation's own logic in isolation. Both sub-clauses verified.

AC8 (8a/8b/8c): masked_reveal_text_test.dart's single widget test asserts find.text(secret) is findsNothing and the masked bullet string is findsOneWidget BEFORE any tap (8a); after tapping visibility, find.text(secret) is findsOneWidget (8b); after tapping visibility_off then calling controller.reveal() DIRECTLY (bypassing the UI, specifically to rule out 'the icon becomes disabled/absent so a real regression would go undetected'), asserts phase stays locked and the real value is still not rendered (8c) -- this is the exact clause flagged in the dispatch as most likely to be missing, and it is genuinely covered at both the widget and controller level (a second, controller-only test independently asserts reveal()/hide() are no-ops -- no notifyListeners call -- once locked). All three sub-clauses verified as independently falsifiable; note the widget test's 8a/8b/8c share one test function rather than three, which is acceptable since each assertion block would independently fail on its own clause's violation (verified by inspection: an 8a regression -- e.g. rendering the secret on first build -- would fail the findsNothing check on line 24 regardless of what the later 8b/8c blocks do).

AC9: confirmed by direct read of docs/mobile/architecture.md -- '## 7. Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment', '**Status: documented now, not implemented in v1 (REQ-422).**', Certificate pinning and Root/jailbreak detection both named and framed as required-before-corporate-tier/not-v1, verified via grep independent of the spec's own quoted excerpt.

AC10: independently re-ran (not trusted from TEST-DESIGNER's quote) from apps/mobile/: `flutter analyze` -> 'No issues found! (ran in 8.7s)'. `flutter test` -> full run, last line 'All tests passed!' at count 86, matching TEST-DESIGNER's quoted 86 exactly (confirmed by reading the full pass/fail line list, including both of AC1's added self-tests present at +65/+66 in the log). SECURITY-REVIEWER PASS (381b2632) and REVIEWER PASS (134a198e) confirmed present in `git log --oneline -5 -- apps/mobile`.

OTHER CHECKS: `grep -rn 'skip:' apps/mobile/test/` -> no matches (no skipped tests anywhere in the suite). `grep -rni TODO apps/mobile/test/` -> no matches. Hardcoded-secret scan (`grep -rniE '(api[_-]?key|password|secret)\s*[:=]'` excluding the deliberate SECRET-TOKEN-SENTINEL/SECRET-REFRESH-SENTINEL/sk_live_ABC123 fixture strings the dispatch explicitly excludes) -> no matches; the sentinel/fixture strings present are exactly the deliberate fake values the acceptance criteria call for, not real secrets. Test isolation: every test file that touches secure storage assigns a FRESH `FlutterSecureStoragePlatform.instance = FakeSecureStoragePlatform()` in its own `setUp()` (tenant_switch_test.dart, transport_policy_test.dart, audience_scoping_test.dart) or inline at the start of its own test body (token_redaction_test.dart) -- confirmed FakeSecureStoragePlatform holds only a per-instance `Map<String,String> _values`, no static/shared state, so no cross-test pollution is possible. Every test constructs its own fakeAdapter/tokenStore/activeRealm locally; no shared global fixtures with hardcoded cross-test IDs. Tests are self-sufficient: each test file's own setUp (or inline setup) fully initializes state needed for that test; no test relies on another test's side effect (verified by reading each file's setUp block and confirming no reference to prior-test-only state).

This is a WF-02 Step 3b test-design gate for a new requirement (MOB-5), not a WF-03 regression test -- the WF-03 'pre-fix failure'/mutant-isolation rule for the 'code under test did not exist' case does not apply here; noted for completeness since the dispatch's role-file boilerplate references it.

No gap found in any of AC1-AC10's decomposed clauses. TEST-DESIGNER's one self-reported gap (AC1/1b) was verified as genuinely closed by the two added self-tests, both independently confirmed falsifiable above. PASS.
